WASHINGTON, Sept 25 : Kansas City Fed President Jeff Schmid said that as the artificial intelligence boom unfolds it will be important for the Fed to understand if the network of firms and contracts developing in the industry is becoming so large it is too big to fail.
"Where we have to start to really synthesize what's happening in the AI and the data center build-out is are we moving to a too-big-to-fail AI ecosystem," he said, referring to the need for public bailouts of major financial institutions during the 2007 to 2009 financial crisis because of their size and influence on the broader economy.
"You worry a little bit about how do we understand what's inside. ... Is there anything systemic?" he asked.

items.title: ハイパースケーラーAI投資、来年は5割増の1.2兆ドルに－ゴールドマン
items.author: Bloomberg
items.creator: Bloomberg
items.summary: （ブルームバーグ）：
items.body:
（ブルームバーグ）： 米国の大手ハイパースケーラー5社によるAIインフラへの支出は、来年に5割超増加し、1兆2000億ドル（約188兆円）に達する見通しだ。ゴールドマン・サックス・グループのストラテジストが明らかにした。

ライアン・ハモンド氏率いるチームはリポートで、この数字は2027年の設備投資についての市場予想1兆1000億ドルを上回ると指摘。各社が投資を回収するには、今後数年間に年間約3000億ドルのAI関連収入が必要になるとの見方を示した。

ハモンド氏らは「市場予想に基づくと、2027年の設備投資が国内総生産（GDP）に占める割合は、1800年代後半の鉄道建設以来、どの技術投資サイクルよりも高くなる見通しだ」と指摘した。

アマゾン・ドット・コム、アルファベット、マイクロソフト、オラクル、メタ・プラットフォームズの5社は今年、AI能力の拡充に8000億ドルを投じる見通しだ。来年の支出額は大幅に増えるものの、設備投資の拡大ペースは鈍化する見込みだと、ゴールドマンのチームは指摘した。

ストラテジストは「設備投資の伸び率と市場予想に対する上振れの度合いはいずれも、ここ数四半期に比べて低下する」と記した。ハイパースケーラーの設備投資は現在、営業キャッシュフローを上回っており、債券発行や株式による資金調達の必要性が高まっている。電力や労働力、メモリーの不足に加え、データセンター建設への規制が制約要因となる可能性がある。

ストラテジストは、ハイパースケーラーの設備投資の伸び率が今年の約100%から2027年には54%、2028年には12%に鈍化すると予想している。2028年の設備投資額は1兆4000億ドルに達する見通しだ。

ハイパースケーラーが十分な投資収益を確保し、アプリケーション事業者もコンピューティング費用に対して高い利益率を得るには、AI利用者がアプリケーションに年間約1兆ドルを支出する必要があると、ストラテジストらは指摘した。2026年の世界のソフトウエア支出は約1兆5000億ドルだった。

items.title: トランプ氏、対加通商交渉に満足　「急ぐ理由ない」＝ＵＳＴＲ代表
items.author: ロイター
items.creator: ロイター
items.summary:
David Shepardson

[ワシントン ２５日 ロイター] -
items.body:
David Shepardson

[ワシントン ２５日 ロイター] - グリア米通商代表部（ＵＳＴＲ）代表は２５日、ＣＮＢＣに対し、対カナダ通商交渉について、トランプ大統領は現状に満足していると述べた。来週にはカナダ製品を対象とした新たな米輸入禁止措置が発効し、米政府は来年１月からカナダ製の自動車、部品、鉄鋼に５０％の関税を課すと警告しているが、トランプ政権はカナダとの通商対立を維持することに問題はなく、米国側に急ぐ理由はないとした。

この発言は、米政府が譲歩の必要をほとんど感じていないことを示している。 

米国が近く導入する輸入禁止措置は、アルコール飲料、オートバイ、乳製品を含む幅広いカナダ製品が対象。１月の関税５０％への引き上げは、北米の自動車生産に重大な影響を及ぼす可能性がある。

一方、カナダによる米製品への報復関税は今月に入って発効した。

グリア代表は「石油、ガス、カリ肥料など、必要なものは依然としてカナダから得られている。農産物も国境を越えて相互に出荷しており、両国間には引き続き活発な貿易がある」と述べた。その上で「われわれは現状に満足している。カナダは時折こちらに連絡してきて、合意の可能性について良好な対話を行っているが、米国側に急ぐ理由はないと言える」と語った。

在ワシントンのカナダ大使館は現時点でコメントしていない。

一部の専門家は、トランプ政権がまずメキシコとの合意を目指しているとみている。これによりカナダとより有利な合意を結ぶための交渉力が高まる可能性があるためという。メキシコ当局者は今週、メキシコとの次回交渉が１０月に行われる可能性があると述べた。

items.title: 米消費者マインド指数、4カ月ぶり低水準－物価高や先行きを懸念
items.author: Bloomberg
items.creator: Bloomberg
items.summary: （ブルームバーグ）：
items.body:
（ブルームバーグ）： 米ミシガン大学が発表した9月の消費者マインド指数（確報値）は前月から低下し、4カ月ぶりの低水準となった。物価上昇や景気の先行きに対する懸念が強まった。

消費者マインド悪化の背景には、ディーゼル価格が過去最高を記録し、ガソリン価格も上昇したことがある。給油時の負担増が、生活費を巡る労働者の根強い不満に拍車をかけている。

インフレが高止まりし、物価の伸びは賃金の伸びを上回っている。住宅ローン金利は7%超に急上昇し、多くの人にとって住宅取得が一段と困難になっている。

ミシガン大の消費者調査ディレクター、ジョアン・シュー氏は発表文で、「政治的な立場の違いにかかわらず、消費者は一様に景気の先行きが悪化したとみている」と指摘した。

今年に入り、消費者マインド指数は年齢や学歴、地域、支持政党、所得のいずれの層でも低下している。

1年先の景気見通しを示す指数は9月に急低下し、2022年以来の低水準となった。家計の先行きに対する見方も悪化した。

耐久財の購入環境は小幅に改善したが、「今のうちに購入を済ませれば、将来の値上がりを避けられるとの消費者の見方」を一部反映したものだとシュー氏は分析した。

原題：US Consumer Sentiment Falls on Worries About Prices, Economy (1)（抜粋）

items.title: 再送「強い円が望ましいとの認識で一致」、日米財務相が電話会談
items.author: ロイター
items.creator: ロイター
items.summary:
(見出しを修正します)

［東京　２５日　ロイター］ -
items.body:
(見出しを修正します)

［東京　２５日　ロイター］ - 日本の財務省は、片山さつき財務相とベセント米財務長官が日本時間の２５日夜、電話で会談したと発表した。同省の声明によると、両氏は円の過小評価が懸念事項であることを改めて確認。金融市場の動向等に関して意見交換を行い、両国間の協力をさらに強化していくことも再確認したという。    

一方、ベセント長官もＸへの投稿で、片山財務相との電話会談は有意義なものだったと表明。日本の力強い経済のファンダメンタルズを反映した強い円が望ましいことや、為替市場について緊密な意思疎通を続けることの重要性を協議したと述べた。

また、今回の電話会談は、今週行われたトランプ大統領と高市首相の協議を踏まえたもので、日米パートナーシップの強固さを反映するものだったと説明した。

これを受け、外国為替市場では円がドルに対して上げ幅を拡大。円は対ドルで１．０９％高の１ドル＝１５７．１３円と、４日続落に終止符を打ち、１日としては９月７日以来最大の上昇率となる見通しとなった。

PARIS, Sept 25 : The organisers of the prestigious Goncourt literary prize said on Friday they had removed a smash-hit novel by Haitian-Canadian author Thelyson Orelien from their longlist after accusations he used AI to write it.
Orelien denied using AI to write "C'etait Ca ou Mourir" ("It Was Either That or Die") as the allegations ignited a debate about race, literary merit and originality that has roiled the French literary establishment.
The accusations about AI use were made this week by a little-known X account "Balance ton Claude." Essayist Samuel Fitoussi later claimed ownership of the account, saying he managed it with other unidentified individuals.
The AI accusations were followed by reports that Orelien had committed plagiarism in earlier works. La Presse said that a 2012 short story by Orelien had plagiarized passages from a book by French author Louis Pauwels, while a 2013 opinion piece copied from The Philippine Star newspaper.

Orelien has yet to respond to those accusations, and did not respond to a request for comment on Friday.
The Paris-based Academie Goncourt said it had taken note of the AI and plagiarism accusations, and had decided to remove his novel "to preserve the integrity of the Goncourt Prize and that of the Academie, whose central role is to promote and honour literature written by women and men."
The Academie said it hoped its decision would show it was fully against the "creation of texts generated with the assistance of AI," adding it would make no further comment before October 6, when it will announce its shortlist.
The debut novel by the Haitian-born author tells the story of a Haitian migrant who travels north through Latin America before ending up in Canada. It has won a host of other literary awards, and was due to be translated into multiple languages.
His French and Canadian publishers initially offered Orelien their full support over the AI allegations. They did not respond to requests for comment on Friday.
"Balance ton Claude" said that running passages through AI detection tool Pangram showed the novel "was written almost entirely by artificial intelligence". Some experts say the reliability of AI detection tools is questionable.

items.title: 米ＴＶ各社がホワイトハウス取材再開、習氏訪問で　締め出し巡る訴訟続く
items.author: ロイター
items.creator: ロイター
items.summary: [ワシントン　２５日　ロイター] - 米テレビ各社は２５日、トランプ大統領のホワイトハウスでの行事の取材を再開し、中国の習近平国家主席の訪問について初めて代表取材（プール取材）による生中継が可能となった。一方、米ＣＮＮ、ＭＳ
items.body:
[ワシントン　２５日　ロイター] - 米テレビ各社は２５日、トランプ大統領のホワイトハウスでの行事の取材を再開し、中国の習近平国家主席の訪問について初めて代表取材（プール取材）による生中継が可能となった。一方、米ＣＮＮ、ＭＳ ＮＯＷ、ポリティコに対する取材制限を巡っては、依然として法廷闘争が続いている。 

トランプ氏は先週、虚偽または否定的だと主張する報道を理由にこの３社をホワイトハウスから締め出した。３社は政権を提訴し、連邦地裁は締め出しが違憲の可能性が高いとしてアクセスを直ちに回復するよう命令。３社のアクセスは２４日に復活した。 

ホワイトハウスのテレビ代表取材は、習氏が訪米最終日の２５日にお茶のためホワイトハウスに到着する様子や、両首脳が米国憲法を収蔵する国立公文書館を視察する様子を映像で伝えた。

ＣＮＮ、ＡＢＣ、ＣＢＳ、ＦＯＸニュース、ＮＢＣの５大ネットワークは大統領取材の費用を分担し、輪番で取材してプール映像を他社に提供している。連帯を示すため他ネットワークがカメラ設置を拒否したことで、習氏訪問の最初の２日間はプール取材が行われなかった。

ＣＮＮは２５日夕、トランプ氏の週末のテネシー州訪問に際し、大統領専用機エアフォースワンへの同乗を拒否されたと明らかにした。ホワイトハウスはロイターのコメント要請に直ちに応じなかった。

２５日に習氏のホワイトハウス到着に合わせてプール取材が再開された際、トランプ氏は中国やイラン、自身のメディア排除、そして税金で賄われた自身の大統領職を宣伝する物議を醸す新たなテレビ広告に関する記者団の質問への回答を拒んだ。その後、記者団に謝意を示し、習氏の隣で「公平な報道に感謝する。非常に公平だった。感謝している」と述べた。

ホワイトハウスは、取材アクセス回復に関するコメント要請に応じなかった。

items.title: ECB、要職の後任争いが本格化－シュナーベル氏退任で時間的圧力
items.author: Bloomberg
items.creator: Bloomberg
items.summary: （ブルームバーグ）：
items.body:
（ブルームバーグ）： 欧州中央銀行（ECB）のシュナーベル理事が早期退任の見通しとなったことで、ラガルド総裁の後任を含むECB要職を巡る争いがますます激しくなりそうだ。

ECBは24日、ドイツ出身のシュナーベル氏は任期をまだ1年残す来年1月に理事を退任すると発表した。3カ月余りの間にECB主要ポストに1つ空席ができることを意味しており、各国政府は早急な対応が必要となった。

ラガルド総裁とチーフエコノミストのレーン氏も2027年に退任予定で、総裁自身も早期退任を示唆している。こうした状況から、ECBトップ人事が一括して決定される公算が極めて大きい。年内に予定される3回の欧州連合（EU）首脳会議で、この人事を巡る駆け引きが繰り広げられることになりそうだ。

こうした人事の決定は、2019年にラガルド氏が任命された際と同様に、各国の対立の場となるリスクをはらむ。約3億6000万人の人口を抱えるユーロ圏の金融政策を主導するECB役員会の半数の席が空く事態に、それぞれが自国の候補の起用を求めるためだ。

ベレンベルクのチーフエコノミスト、ホルガー・シュミーディング氏は「ECB人事の決定は、今や時間的なプレッシャーがある」と指摘。「一括した決定は困難だろう。だが、決定が難しくても解決策を見いだすのが政治家の仕事だ」と述べた。

人事決定の期限が迫る一方で、域内大国は政治的に難しい時期にある。ドイツの与党は州議選での敗北が相次ぎ、メルツ政権は存続が危うい状況だ。フランスは来年春の大統領選挙を前に、政治的な行き詰まりに陥っている。イタリア、スペインも総選挙が近い。

EUのあらゆる決定と同様に、こう着状態に陥る危険も排除できない。シュナーベル氏自身、ブルームバーグが入手したECBスタッフに対する別れのメッセージで、その可能性に言及していた。

シュナーベル氏はその中で「後任はEU首脳会議が指名する」と説明。「自分の退任後、自分の責務は必要に応じて役員会の残りメンバーに一時的に割り振られることになるだろう」と続けた。

items.title: 日米財務相が電話会談、ベッセント長官「強い円が望ましい」
items.author: Bloomberg
items.creator: Bloomberg
items.summary: （ブルームバーグ）：
items.body:
（ブルームバーグ）： 片山さつき財務相は日本時間25日夜、ベッセント米財務長官と電話会談を行った。円の過小評価は問題だとの認識を再確認し、日米間の協力をさらに強化していくことをあらためて申し合わせたと、財務省が発表した。

ベッセント長官はその後、「日本の強固な経済ファンダメンタルズを反映した強い円が望ましい」との認識について協議したと、SNSの投稿で明らかにした。

この日は、日本の政策当局者から、政府の経済政策全般に対する市場の見方を意識した発言が相次いだ。円はここ数日、日本銀行の金融政策が円相場をどの程度支えられるかとの懸念が強まる中で下落していた。

ニューヨーク時間同日午前の外国為替市場では、日米財務相の会談が伝わると、円がドルに対して上げ幅を拡大。円は対ドルで一時、前日比1.2%高の1ドル＝156円94銭に上昇した。終盤の取引では157円台前半に上げを縮めている。

高市早苗首相は同日、現地時間22日にニューヨークで実施した日米首脳会談で、一般論として「円の過小評価は問題である」とトランプ米大統領に伝えたと、官邸で記者団に語っていた。会談ではトランプ氏から、円安によって米国の貿易が厳しいとの懸念を示され、回答したという。

ベッセント長官は今回の電話会談について、高市氏とトランプ氏の首脳会談を踏まえたもので、強固な日米関係を反映していると説明。為替市場について緊密な意思疎通を続ける重要性について協議したと述べた。

片山氏は同日午後に行ったブルームバーグのインタビューで、高市氏は金融緩和や財政拡張を志向する「リフレ派｣ではないと強調。日銀の独立性を尊重しているとも述べ、財政運営や金融政策への影響を巡る投資家の懸念を打ち消した。

円安傾向が続く為替市場では、過度に投機的な動きについて「断固たる措置を取る」とこれまでも表明しているとも発言。高市、トランプ両政権下では「行動をとることに躊躇（ちゅうちょ）しないとまで言っている」と話した。

BANGKOK, Sept 25 : Thailand's economy is expected to retain its momentum and grow by 2.5 per cent next year and could reach 3 per cent expansion within the next three years, the finance minister said on Friday, as the government pushes for new investments into key sectors.  
Ekniti Nitithanprapas told Reuters he was confident of achieving 2.5 per cent economic expansion in 2027, in what was his first growth projection for next year.
Top of the government's agenda, he said, was to court more foreign and domestic investment, including in niche semiconductor segments. 
"In my opinion, growth might be likely to be higher than what maybe the Bank of Thailand or other people forecasted," he said in an interview two weeks out from the annual meetings of the International Monetary Fund and World Bank, taking place in Bangkok.

"We need to keep pushing domestic investment to grow further and reduce reliance on export sectors." 
Last week, assistant central bank governor Don Nakornthab told Reuters the bank was maintaining its growth forecasts of 2.3 per cent for this year and 1.8 per cent for 2027. He put potential growth at 2.7 per cent and said it could take four to five years to return to that rate.
INFLATION AND BAHT VOLATILITY
Southeast Asia's second-largest economy expanded 1.9 per cent year-on-year in the second quarter, down sharply from 2.8 per cent growth in the previous quarter. The economy, which grew 2.4 per cent last year, has been struggling with weak productivity, subdued demand, high household debt and low investment.
Ekniti said he was not concerned about inflation, which should stay within 3 per cent this year and next, while the weaker baht might be better for the Thai economy but should not be volatile.
The baht has weakened by 5.6 per cent against the US dollar so far this year. 
Headline inflation accelerated to 2.53 per cent in August but within the central bank's 1 per cent to 3 per cent target range.  
The government's consumer subsidy scheme, which has been in operation for four months, would account for 0.4 per cent to 0.5 per cent of GDP growth in 2026, Ekniti said.
The scheme was this week extended through to November, with 43 billion baht ($1.29 billion) allocated, part of a broader 400 billion baht borrowing programme. 
"We target to give subsidies to help people affected by the rising cost of living. So that's why we expect it to be short-term," said Ekniti, who is also deputy prime minister. 
"We plan to lower it down, and we're trying to push investments going forward."
NICHE SEMICONDUCTORS
Thailand is targeting $80 billion in semiconductor investment by 2050 and more than 230,000 new jobs under a national strategy announced on Thursday, which aims to build a fully integrated domestic chip ecosystem and generate $150 billion in annual revenue.
"We are quite good in photonics. We are quite good in sensing and power units. So we aim to move in that direction," he said.
"We will provide lots of incentives, work with private sector so that we can bring in more investment."
Ekniti said the government was also working with the central bank to try to boost credit access to small businesses.
The public debt-to-GDP ratio would rise to 68 per cent to 69 per cent this year, he added, but still under the 70 per cent ceiling. 
A positive factor for Thailand was its political stability, he said.
"Never before have we had good coalition parties with only two parties," he said. "That could provide stability for the government to continue credible policies." 
($1 = 33.3200 baht)

items.title: 米コア資本財受注、8月は1.6％増と予想上回る　ＡＩ投資が下支え
items.author: ロイター
items.creator: ロイター
items.summary: [ワシントン　２５日　ロイター] -
items.body:
[ワシントン　２５日　ロイター] - 米商務省が２５日発表した８月の耐久財受注は、民間設備投資の先行指標とされるコア資本財（非国防資本財から航空機を除く）の受注が前月比１．６％増加した。ロイターがまとめたエコノミスト予想（０．５％増）を上回る伸びとなり、人工知能（ＡＩ）関連インフラの構築を背景に、企業の設備投資が今四半期も堅調に拡大していることを示唆した。 

７月は０．６％増と、速報値の変わらずから上方改定された。

８月は前年同月比では１０．６％増加した。

項目別の受注は、電気機器・家電・部品が１．１％増と伸びを主導した。コンピューター・関連製品は１．５％急増し、前年同月比では２０．１％増となった。通信機器は０．３％増、前年同月比では３５．８％急増した。

機械は１．１％、一次金属は１．２％それぞれ増加。一方、金属加工品は１．３％減少した。

自動車・部品は０．６％減。民間航空機は４．３％減となった。米航空機大手ボーイングのウェブサイトによると、８月の航空機受注数は１５機。７月は３８機だった。   

非国防資本財の受注は１．２％増加した。

耐久財受注全体は７月の０．９％増から８月は横ばいとなった。輸送機器の受注が０．６％減少したことが重しとなった。耐久財受注はトースターから航空機まで３年以上使われるモノを指す。 

８月のコア資本財の出荷は０．６％増。７月は１．４％増だった。

非国防資本財の出荷は１．３％減となった。

企業の設備投資は、ＡＩ関連の積極的な投資に支えられ２四半期連続で２桁の伸びを記録しており、製造業および経済全体を下支えしている。ただエコノミストらは、原油価格や金利、米長期債利回りの上昇を背景に、特にＡＩと関連の薄い分野の製造業が減速する可能性があると警鐘を鳴らしている。

ＦＷＤＢＯＮＤＳのチーフエコノミスト、クリストファー・ラプキー氏は「ＡＩ投資ブームは本物であり、経済全体をけん引している」と指摘。その上で「唯一のリスクは、いずれ全ての設備投資とデータセンターの建設が完了し、このＡＩバブルが膨張し切った後の成長要因が不透明であることだ。投資支出は成長の加速要因と見なされているが、いずれ終わりは必ず来る」と述べた。

items.title: TV networks resume covering White House as press access fight continues
items.author: Susan Heavey
items.creator: Susan Heavey
items.summary: US television networks resumed coverage of President Donald Trump’s White House events on Friday, providing the first live pool access for Chinese President Xi Jinping’s visit, as a legal battle continues over restrictions on CNN, MS NOW and Politico.
items.body:
US television networks resumed coverage of President Donald Trump ’s White House events on Friday, providing the first live pool access for Chinese President Xi Jinping’s visit, as a legal battle continues over restrictions on CNN, MS NOW and Politico.
Trump last week banned the three outlets from the White House, before a judge ordered the administration to [USN:L1N45G0ZE TEXT:"restore their access"].
The White House television press pool aired video of Xi's arrival at the White House for tea on the final day of the Chinese leader's visit, as well as the two leaders' [USN:L8N45G1YG TEXT:"tour of the National Archives"], which houses the US Constitution.
CNN, ABC, CBS, Fox News and NBC share the costs of covering the president and rotate coverage, providing pool footage to other outlets. The other networks' refusal to set up cameras in solidarity meant there was no pool coverage of the first two days of Xi's visit.
CNN on Friday evening said it had been barred from traveling with Trump on Air Force One for a weekend trip to Tennessee. The White House did not immediately respond to a request for comment from Reuters.
Trump has long relied on the media to shape his public image and advance his agenda, even as he regularly casts news organizations as political adversaries. Since returning to office last year, his administration has taken an aggressive stance against major news outlets, including limiting access to the Oval Office and other restricted spaces.
As pool coverage resumed for Xi's arrival at the White House on Friday, Trump declined to answer questions from reporters on China and Iran, his media ban and a controversial new taxpayer-funded TV ad that promotes his presidency. He later thanked reporters.
"We appreciate the fair coverage. It's been very fair. We appreciate it," Trump later told reporters alongside Xi.
The White House did not respond to a request for comment about the restored press access.
UNPRECEDENTED CAMPAIGN [USN:L8N45A1OV TEXT:"Trump banned the three news outlets"] from the White House complex over coverage he asserted was false or negative. Their access was reinstated on Thursday, after a federal judge deemed [USN:L8N45A1OV TEXT:"the ban"] likely unconstitutional and ordered their access to be immediately restored.
CNN, MS NOW and Politico sued Trump and other members of his administration, saying the ban violated the US Constitution's First Amendment protections for free speech and a free press, as well as their due process rights. A coalition of press freedom groups and dozens of news organizations, including Reuters, later filed a legal brief supporting the action.
Despite the temporary ruling restoring access, the court has not yet resolved the main challenge to the ban, based on the First Amendment of the US Constitution that protects the right to free speech and a free press. The news outlets now have until September 28 to ask the judge to keep their access in place while the case moves forward.
Even if the outlets won a permanent injunction against the ban, [USN:L1N45G0ZE TEXT:"Trump could still pursue his case"] in federal court.
Trump has waged an unprecedented campaign against the media since returning to office last year, launching personal attacks on journalists, denying access to some outlets and suing news organizations, as well as calling on the Federal Communications Commission to strip broadcast stations of their licenses.
FRIENDLIEST PRESS CORPS On Thursday, Trump made a joke to photographers in the Oval Office about China -- which imposes strict censorship across its media -- having the friendliest press corps, as he welcomed Xi to the White House.
While the White House on Thursday told the court it had reinstated CNN, MS NOW and Politico's access, CNN and MS NOW later said some of their journalists were denied access to cover Xi's arrival for the White House state dinner, according to the Washington Post.
A lawyer for the three outlets in court this week warned that the White House could again try to revoke the outlets' White House access as the current litigation continues.
David Ellison, CEO of Paramount Skydance (PSKY.O) , which is seeking to merge with CNN-parent Warner Bros. Discovery (WBD.O) , attended the [USN:L6N45G1DV TEXT:"Trump-Xi state dinner"] Thursday night.
Critics have raised concerns about Paramount-owned CBS News tailoring coverage to favor Trump, although Ellison has promised to create an [USN:L4N45E0EO TEXT:"editorial independence board"] for both CBS and CNN as part of the deal.

items.title: 円が対ドルで3週ぶり大幅高、156円94銭－日米財務相が円安巡り協議
items.author: Bloomberg
items.creator: Bloomberg
items.summary: （ブルームバーグ）：
items.body:
（ブルームバーグ）： ニューヨーク時間25日の外国為替市場で、円がドルに対して上げ幅を拡大した。日米財務相が同日に電話会談を行い、円の過小評価は問題だとの認識を再確認したと、日本の財務省が発表した。

円は対ドルで一時、ニューヨーク前日比1.2%高の1ドル＝156円94銭を付けた。9月7日以来、約3週間ぶりの大幅な上昇率となった。円は他の主要10通貨全てに対して上昇している。

発表資料によれば、片山さつき財務相とベッセント米財務長官は金融市場の動向などに関して意見を交換し、日米間の協力を一段と強化することで一致した。

円はそれ以前、片山氏が25日の会見で、日米首脳会談では「トランプ米大統領から円安への懸念が示された」と述べたことなどを受けて、既に上昇していた。

高市早苗首相も、一般論として「円の過小評価は問題である」とトランプ氏に首脳会談で伝えたと記者団に述べた。

ノムラ・インターナショナルの通貨ストラテジスト、宮入祐輔氏は、日米首脳会談後、政府高官から立て続けに出てきた発言を見ると「円安是正に向けた米国からの圧力は強いと感じる」と指摘。

「1ドル＝160円を超えてのドル・円上昇を期待していた一部の市場参加者の意欲を大きくそぐものとなり、それが、この日の円ショートカバーにつながった」との見解を示した。

ベッセント氏はまた、「日本の強固な経済ファンダメンタルズを反映した強い円が望ましい」との認識について片山氏と協議したと、SNSの投稿で明らかにした。

これについて宮入氏は、金融政策に関して、トランプ大統領からではないにせよ、引き続きベッセント氏から注文が入った可能性を指摘した。高市首相は25日、日米首脳会談では「金融政策、財政政策に関する議論はなかった」と記者団に語っていた。

宮入氏は「今後のドル・円相場は引き続き155－160円の大きなレンジの中で推移する」と予想し、「介入に関しては160円を超える円安になってからとみている」と述べた。

items.author: Bloomberg
items.creator: Bloomberg
items.summary: （ブルームバーグ）：
items.body:
（ブルームバーグ）： ニューヨーク時間25日午前の外国為替市場で、円がドルに対して上げ幅を拡大した。日米財務相が同日に電話会談を行い、円の過小評価は問題だとの認識を再確認したと、日本の財務省が発表した。

円は対ドルで一時、ニューヨーク前日比1.2%高の1ドル＝156円94銭を付けた。これは約3週間ぶりの大幅な上昇率。円は他の主要10通貨全てに対して上昇している。

発表資料によれば、片山さつき財務相とベッセント米財務長官は金融市場の動向などに関して意見を交換し、日米間の協力を一段と強化することで一致した。

円はそれ以前、片山氏が同日の会見で、日米首脳会談では「トランプ米大統領から円安への懸念が示された」と述べたことなどを受けて、既に上昇していた。

高市早苗首相もその後、一般論として「円の過小評価は問題である」とトランプ氏に首脳会談で伝えたことを明らかにした。

一連の発言を受け、円相場を支えるために当局が介入に踏み切るリスクに対して警戒感が高まっている。

オーバーシー・チャイニーズ銀行の為替ストラテジスト、モー・シオン・シム氏は「介入リスクが円安のさらなる進行に歯止めをかけるだろう」と予測。重要なのは「トランプ氏の懸念が円を支えるための日米間の緊密な連携を示唆しており、円相場は転換点に近づいている可能性があるという点だ」と語った。

円には再び下押し圧力がかかっていた。米連邦準備制度理事会（FRB）が追加利上げに動くとの観測から、日米の金利差が大きく開いた状態が続くとの見方が強まっているためだ。日本銀行がどの程度のペースで利上げを続けられるかを巡る不透明感も円の重しとなっている。

STOCKHOLM, Sept 25 : An expected European Union vote on allowing Tesla's supervised Full Self-Driving system across the bloc has been delayed from October, with the next apparent opportunity for a decision not before December, according to an agenda published on the EU's website.
• Dutch regulator RDW approved the system in April, with Belgium and a handful of other countries following suit
• RDW is also proposing that the software be approved across the bloc
• Tesla said on September 1 in a post on X that an EU-wide vote could potentially happen on October 6

• However, the agenda for an October 6 meeting of the Technical Committee on Motor Vehicles (TCMV), which brings together representatives of EU member states and the European Commission, lists only a "continuation of discussions" on the Dutch request for an Article 39 authorisation, with 25 minutes allocated to the discussion
• RDW told Reuters it would not speculate on the discussion, the vote or any potential outcome.
• Tesla did not respond to a request for comment. In response to a post on X about the delayed vote, CEO Elon Musk wrote: "sigh"
• The committee has already discussed Tesla's request at two previous meetings. The next scheduled TCMV meeting after October is in December, making that the earliest apparent opportunity for a vote based on the current agenda
• An EU-wide rollout requires support by a "qualified majority" of 15 of the EU's 27 member states, representing 65 per cent of the bloc's population
• Several EU countries, including Sweden, have expressed concerns about FSD exceeding speed limits, while countries that approved it say drivers remain responsible for complying with traffic laws
• The same committee approved Ford's BlueCruise driver assistance system March 2024, with Germany as its sponsor
• Tesla has called FSD approval key to boosting sales in Europe, where it is seeking to regain market share amid growing competition from Chinese electric-vehicle makers

Can AI produce para-athletes? Finalists from AP, Telangana, Tamil Nadu, Odisha are among young innovators

Samsung Solve for Tomorrow is a global initiative where students use technology to solve community challenges.

Sakshi Mehra

New Delhi: Eight young innovators from Andhra Pradesh, Telangana, Tamil Nadu and Odisha have reached the Top 20 of the Samsung Solve for Tomorrow 2026 competition. They bring five technology-based ideas aimed at improving para-sports, athlete performance, swimming safety and exercise support for people with Parkinson’s disease.  

Samsung Solve for Tomorrow is an innovation competition where students use STEM to solve community challenges. In its fifth edition in India, Samsung Solve for Tomorrow has four themes: AI Living for India, Health & Education, Environmental Sustainability, and Sport & Tech.

The eight innovators — Pasupuleti Ruthvik, Kolla Venkata Siva Surya, Homanshika Reddy Pullagurla, Vatala Harika, Ritesh Routray, Manoj Kumar Kasinathan, Jena R and Chriswin William D — are part of a national Top 20 cohort representing 18 cities across 12 states.

Show Full Article

More than half of the finalists come from Tier 2 and Tier 3 cities, Samsung said. The Top 20 teams are now receiving mentorship and support to develop prototypes. Four winning teams will collectively receive Rs 2 crore in grants and incubation support from FITT-IIT Delhi.

Making swimming safer for visually impaired athletes
Two of the five projects focus on challenges faced by visually impaired swimmers.

Pasupuleti Ruthvik, 21, from Chittoor developed Untethered, a wearable sensor system designed to alert swimmers when they are approaching the end of a pool lane.

For visually impaired swimmers, reaching the wall without a visual cue can be difficult and may result in head injuries. Ruthvik’s system provides real-time alerts, reducing dependence on manual cues from coaches and allowing swimmers to train more independently.

Kolla Venkata Siva Surya, 16, from Visakhapatnam, is working on a different challenge: maintaining direction inside the lane. His assistive trajectory system detects when a swimmer begins to move away from the intended path and provide real-time feedback, allowing the swimmer to correct their trajectory.

Also Read: Samsung turned first foldable iPhone launch into a roast. Apple fans are hitting back

Using AI to identify para-sport talent
In Sundargarh, Vatala Harika, 21, and Ritesh Routray, 20, are using AI to identify para-athletes. 

Their project, ParaSync, is an AI-based platform that assesses adaptive sporting techniques and identifies promising athletes. It also aims to connect them with professional coaching and competitive opportunities.

The project is based on the idea that sporting talent can emerge outside established sporting centres, where athletes may have fewer opportunities to access formal training and competition.

Wearables for safer exercise and training
In Chennai, Manoj Kumar Kasinathan, 21, Jena R, 20, and Chriswin William D, 20, are developing Rogue, a wearable device aimed at supporting exercise for people with Parkinson’s disease.

In Hyderabad, 21-year-old Homanshika Reddy Pullagurla is developing Somatrace, an IoT-enabled wearable designed to monitor spinal load among precision-sport athletes.

The device tracks movement and physical load in real time, helping athletes understand the strain their bodies experience during training and how they respond to different movements.

The eight innovators took part in a prototyping programme with FITT-IIT Delhi that included an Innovation Bootcamp and online mentoring from Samsung experts.

The programme helped them understand users’ needs, develop prototypes, identify potential markets, and understand the impact and scalability of their ideas.

They also visited Samsung Design Delhi, Samsung R&D Institute India facilities in Noida, Delhi, and Bengaluru, and Samsung’s headquarters in Gurugram.

Now in its fifth edition in India, Samsung Solve for Tomorrow has four themes: AI Living for India, Health & Education, Environmental Sustainability, and Sport & Tech.

items.title: 中国はイラン支援せずと確約、トランプ氏が習主席に警告＝駐中国米大使
items.author: ロイター
items.creator: ロイター
items.summary:
Bo Erickson　Susan Heavey　Katharine Jackson　Parisa Hafezi

［ワシントン　２５日　ロイター］ -
items.body:
Bo Erickson　Susan Heavey　Katharine Jackson　Parisa Hafezi

［ワシントン　２５日　ロイター］ - トランプ米大統領は２４日に行った中国の習近平国家主席との会談で、中国によるイラン支援は容認できないと明確に伝え、習主席は支援しないと確約した。米国のパデュー駐中国大使が２５日、明らかにした。

パデュー大使はＣＮＢＣのインタビューで「数週間前、イランへのいかなる支援も、直接か間接かを問わず、情報、部品、軍事装備のいずれであっても、全く容認できないと中国側に明確に伝えた」とした上で「トランプ大統領は昨日、あらためてこの点を非常に明確にした。このメッセージは継続的に発信している」と述べた。

ＦＯＸニュースの番組で、こうした状況は中国によるイラン支援停止を意味するのかとの質問に対し、「すでに動きが見られる。中国側は２４日、支援はしないとわれわれに保証した」と応じた。

パデュー氏はまたＣＮＢＣとのインタビューで、トランプ氏と習氏について「一定の信頼関係を築き始め、諸問題に取り組んでいる」と指摘。「非常に率直で開かれた会談だった」とし、両首脳が話すたびに、取り組んでいる懸案を巡り、より踏み込んだ意思疎通ができていると感じると語った。

トランプ大統領もこの日、習主席との会談でイラン情勢について協議したと確認。ただ、詳細は明らかにしなかった。

items.title: 米コア資本財の受注が予想を上回る－設備投資に依然勢い
items.author: Bloomberg
items.creator: Bloomberg
items.summary: （ブルームバーグ）：
items.body:
（ブルームバーグ）： 8月の米耐久財受注統計（速報値）では、ビジネス機器の受注が予想を上回る伸びを示した。設備投資の勢いが続いていることが浮き彫りになった。

耐久財統計では、一次金属、機械、コンピューター、電気機器の受注が増加した。自動車と民間航空機の受注が減少し、輸送機器の受注は落ち込んだ。

今年はAI関連の支出にけん引され、設備投資と需要が堅調に推移している。企業による機器への設備投資は今年上期の国内総生産（GDP）の伸びに大きく寄与した。

この統計に先立って発表されたアトランタ連銀の予想モデル「GDPナウ」は、設備投資が第3四半期の成長率を1ポイント近く押し上げるとしていた。堅調な個人消費と合わせ、今回の耐久財統計は第3四半期も経済が力強く成長する下地が整っていることを示した。

航空機を含む非国防資本財の出荷は前月から1.3%減少した。これはGDP統計の設備投資項目に直接反映される。政府は取り消しが可能な受注ではなく、出荷データをGDPの算出に用いている。

ただ、今回の統計によるとコア資本財の出荷は0.6%増と、過去2カ月の大幅な伸びを下回った。

ブルームバーグ・エコノミクスのエコノミスト、エリザ・ウィンガー氏は「コア受注と出荷は、設備投資が第3四半期のGDP成長率に大きく寄与することを示唆している。AI関連支出に加え、より有利な税制環境が引き続き投資の勢いを支えている」と分析した。

エコノミストは基調的な設備投資を見極める上で、コア資本財の出荷を重視している。航空機や軍事関連は、受注から実際の出荷まで極めて長い時間がかかるためだ。

月ごとの変動が大きい民間航空機の受注は4.3%減少した。ボーイングは8月の受注が15機と、前月の38機から減少したと明らかにした。

items.title: Pope Leo warns that AI is creating 'paradise of machines'
items.author: CNA
items.summary: Pope Leo says "there is an urgent need for education in ethical discernment".
items.body:

Pope Leo warns that AI is creating 'paradise of machines'

 Pope Leo says "there is an urgent need for education in ethical discernment".

Pope Leo delivers a speech during a meeting with French President Emmanuel Macron and authorities, members of civil society and the diplomatic corps at the Elysee Palace in Paris as part of his four-day apostolic journey to France, on Sep 25, 2026. (Photo: REUTERS/Benoit Tessier/Pool)

(Updated: 25 Sep 2026 09:04PM)

FAST

PARIS: Pope Leo urged the world to reconsider the development of artificial intelligence , opening his four-day visit to France on Friday (Sep 25) with a fervent warning that AI could create a future where "a paradise of machines" takes control of the Earth.
The first US pope, who has made sounding the alarm about the risks of AI a central part of his 16-month papacy, put the issue at the heart of his visit to France, the first by a pope in nearly 20 years.
"If we are to avoid losing our humanity amid a 'paradise of machines' invading and conditioning our daily lives, there is an urgent need for education in ethical discernment," he said, speaking under the gilded ceilings of the Elysee Palace.
The pope also strongly reiterated the Church's pro-life teachings, criticising initiatives to allow assisted dying for those who have incurable illnesses, two months after French politicians approved such a measure.

"I am concerned … by those trends in society that risk turning science and technology into profit-driven ventures promoting genetic manipulation, surrogacy, the trade in human organs or the possibility of arranging one’s own death," he said.
The pope, on a whirlwind three-city visit to France, will also seek to repair the Church's standing there after abuse scandals sparked nationwide shock, and is also expected to lay out a vision for the future of Europe in a speech on Monday.

Pope Leo XIV walks on a red carpet toward France's President Emmanuel Macron and his wife Brigitte Macron ahead of a meeting at the Elysee Presidential Palace, in Paris on Sep 25, 2026, at the start of his four days visit to France. (Photo: Remo Casilli/POOL/AFP)

"MESSAGE OF PEACE" The pope was greeted at the Paris Orly airport, under a clear blue sky, by President Emmanuel Macron and his wife Brigitte, and by children who sang for him and asked for autographs. During his visit, he will travel to the famed Catholic shrine at Lourdes, in the southwest, and to Metz, on the German border.
Pope Leo was due to lead a prayer service in Paris on Friday at the restored Notre-Dame cathedral, in the first visit by a pope since a devastating fire nearly destroyed the Gothic masterpiece in 2019.
Telling reporters on the plane to Paris that he was coming to convey a message of peace, he added: "It is a message which at this time, as we all may know, is particularly important."
People lining the streets Pope Leo was due to pass through on his way to the Elysee held up phones and waved flags and signs.
"He brings a message of peace and hope that is very, very positive. His visit to France sends a wonderful signal to the country," a Catholic passer-by, Antoine Barxias-Casties, said in front of Notre-Dame cathedral on the eve of Pope Leo's visit.
Next on the pope's agenda on Friday is a speech to staff at the headquarters of the UN culture and education body, UNESCO, which is facing budget shortfalls after US President Donald Trump withdrew from the agency in 2025.
The first US pope attracted Trump's ire earlier this year after criticising the Iran war.
Asked about Trump's attempt to bar CNN and several other outlets from the White House, Pope Leo, aboard the plane to Paris, reaffirmed his support for freedom of the press, saying all were welcome to cover his visit.

France's President Emmanuel Macron (L) welcomes Pope Leo XIV (R) ahead of a meeting at the Elysee Presidential Palace, in Paris on Sep 25, 2026 at the start of his four days visit to France. (Photo: Teresa Suarez/POOL/AFP)

SECULAR NATION France, a secular nation where the separation of church and state is enshrined in a 1905 law, has witnessed a steady decline in affiliation to the Catholic Church during the post-war era, mirroring a trend in other traditionally Catholic countries.
Although the French Bishops' Conference points to an increase in baptisms of adults, a report published by the official statistics agency INSEE showed that only 25 per cent of French 18-to-49-year-olds identified as Catholic, compared with 43 per cent a decade earlier.
Pope Leo's visit comes as Catholic leaders in France have been at odds with the government over the 2024 enshrining of a right to abortion in the French constitution, a world first, and the passage of the law legalising assisted dying for adults with incurable illnesses.
POPE TO MEET ABUSE SURVIVORS Local Church leaders hope the pope's visit will repair the Church's standing after a crushing 2021 report found that some 330,000 French children had been abused by Catholic clergy and lay leaders over seven decades.
French bishops have since introduced compensation and safeguarding measures, but survivors have continued to press Church leaders to demonstrate accountability.
"Leo bears the immense responsibility of 'declaring enough is enough'," Alain Esquerre, 66, a spokesperson for victims at the Notre-Dame de Bétharram Catholic institution, told Reuters.
The pope will meet seven French victims of abuse by Catholic clergy on Sunday in Lourdes.

FAST

Sept 25 : Microsoft on Friday unveiled several new capabilities in its Copilot app, including a coding tool and an always-on AI agent, as the software giant seeks to transform its AI assistant into a one-stop shop for office workers.
The company is also embedding its Office applications Word, Excel, and PowerPoint directly within Copilot, allowing users to work collaboratively on these apps without having to leave the AI tool.
Shares of the Redmond, Washington-based company rose about 3 per cent in early trading.
Microsoft is racing to expand Copilot beyond its chat-based roots to boost adoption as it competes with AI chatbots such as ChatGPT and Claude.

The Windows maker unveiled "Code" to let users build apps, dashboards and other software using natural language prompts. The tool, powered by the same technology as Microsoft's GitHub Copilot, will roll out to early-access customers at the end of the month, while 365 Premium and Pro subscribers can preview it later this year.
Microsoft is also rolling out "Autopilot", a revamp of the "Scout" AI agent it unveiled in June, in a private preview at the end of the month. The so-called digital coworker agent will carry its own identity in the company directory and have specific permissions that users can control.
"I think it's been very hard for many organizations to bring agents into the enterprise because of security, compliance and governance concerns," Annie Pearl, corporate vice president of Copilot Product, said in an interview.
"So we've worked... to make sure that we were building this in a way that would really be able to be used in the enterprise."
Microsoft also unveiled cost-management capabilities to allow employees to have direct insight into costs tied to their AI usage. The move comes at a time when enterprises are increasingly worried about rapid AI usage racking up unexpected costs.

items.title: Number of Sudanese fleeing to Chad surges 20-fold as aid runs dry, UN says
items.author: Olivia Le Poidevin
items.creator: Olivia Le Poidevin
items.summary: There has been a sharp increase in the number of people fleeing from Sudan to Chad to escape fighting and dire conditions, and aid funding is failing to keep up with needs, the United Nations refugee agency said on Friday.
items.body:
There has been a sharp increase in the number of people fleeing from Sudan to Chad to [USN:L6N40Y0KB TEXT:"escape fighting"] and dire conditions, and aid funding is failing to keep up with needs, the United Nations refugee agency said on Friday.
More than 400 people a day have been crossing into eastern Chad over the past week, a 20-fold increase from the numbers seen in recent months, UNHCR said.
They were fleeing Sudan's Darfur, Kordofan and Blue Nile regions — which have all been hit by clashes between Sudan's army and the paramilitary Rapid Support Forces in a more than three-year-old civil war.
There were "people who tell us that they flee the conflict, they flee the aerial bombardments, they flee the drone attacks," Mamadou Dian Balde, UN Regional Refugee Coordinator for the Sudan Situation, told reporters in Geneva via video link from Nairobi.
Only 18% of the $1.6 billion funding it needed this year had come in, UNHCR said.
“It means less food. It means less capacity for people to be relocated to safer areas. It means less capacity to shelter themselves,” Dian Balde said.
The agency warned of potential knock-on effects if Sudanese refugees’ basic needs are not met in Chad, saying its analysis shows many move on towards Europe after repeated failed attempts to find safety.
The civil war has devastated wide swathes of Sudan, displacing up to 14 million people, ruining harvests and decimating the economy, according to UN estimates.
Drought and other harsh conditions were also forcing people to move, UNHCR said.
Almost 1 million refugees have crossed into Chad since the conflict began, more than 55,000 so far this year, according to UNHCR data.
Aid groups like UNHCR face major funding shortfalls after the administration of US President Donald Trump and other donor countries cut billions of dollars in foreign assistance over the past year.

items.title: FRB、大手銀への監督強化巡る基準引き上げを計画－ロイター
items.author: Bloomberg
items.creator: Bloomberg
items.summary: （ブルームバーグ）：
items.body:
（ブルームバーグ）： 米連邦準備制度理事会（FRB）は、大手銀行により厳格な監督を適用する際の基準となる資産額を引き上げる方向で検討を進めている。ロイター通信が匿名の関係者4人の話として報じた。

FRBは、銀行のバランスシートのストレステストや流動性、資本に関する規制の適用基準となる資産額の引き上げを検討している。関係者3人によれば、具体案は年内にも示される可能性がある。

2019年に設定された現行基準では、銀行の資産が1000億ドル（約15兆7600億円）を超えると規制が適用され、2500億ドルと7000億ドルを超えると追加の規制要件が課される。関係者がロイターに語ったところによると、最も低い基準は1500億ドルに、最も高い基準は1兆ドル近くに引き上げられる可能性がある。

基準の引き上げは、JPモルガン・チェースやシティグループなど米最大手銀行には影響しないものの、USバンコープやキャピタル・ワン・ファイナンシャルなどにとっては、最も厳しい規制の対象となるまでの余地が広がるとロイターは報じた。

原題：Fed Plans to Raise Bank Asset Oversight Thresholds, Reuters Says

items.title: ウクライナ財政・国防支援、ＥＵ・ＩＭＦも重要性理解＝大統領
items.author: ロイター
items.creator: ロイター
items.summary: [キーウ ２５日 ロイター] -
items.body:
[キーウ ２５日 ロイター] - ウクライナのゼレンスキー大統領は２５日、欧州連合（ＥＵ）と国際通貨基金（ＩＭＦ）が、ウクライナの財政赤字を補い、国防費を賄うための支援の重要性を理解していると述べた。

ゼレンスキー氏は、１０月と１１月に無人機（ドローン）を発注する必要があり、できなければ来年初めに困難な状況に直面すると語った。

メッセージアプリ「ワッツアップ」を通じた記者会見で「ウクライナだけでは対応できず、ウクライナ製のドローンやミサイルへの投資を増やす必要があることを誰もが理解している」と述べた。ＥＵのフォンデアライエン欧州委員長から前向きな回答を得たとも明らかにした。

ウクライナは国防費だけでなく、社会保障費や人道支援に関する支出も海外からの支援に頼っている。来年は５２０億ドルを超える国際的な資金支援が必要になると見込んでいる。

マルチェンコ財務相は記者団に対し、ウクライナ向け融資プログラムの第２次審査を行うＩＭＦ調査団が１１月に訪問する見通しだと述べた。それまでに来年の予算の財源確保に向けた計画を策定する必要があるとした。

items.title: メッカ防衛協定、イラン参加も可能＝トルコ国会議長
items.author: ロイター
items.creator: ロイター
items.summary: [アンカラ ２５日 ロイター] -
items.body:
[アンカラ ２５日 ロイター] - トルコのクルトゥルムシュ国会議長は２５日、トルコ、サウジアラビア、パキスタンが合意した「メッカ共同防衛協定」について、イランも含む「イスラム世界のための」より広範な協定に発展する可能性があると述べた。

アンカラで記者団に「国際協定の発効には国会の承認が必要だ。現在行われている協定関連の会合は準備段階のものだ」と説明した。国会が１０月に休会明けを迎えることに触れ、「近く審議される見込みだ」と述べた。

協定がイランに対抗するものかとの質問に対し、特定の国を標的としたものではないとするトルコの立場を改めて示した。紛争やイスラエルの「敵対的政策」が続く中、地域諸国の安全確保を主眼に置いたものだと説明した。

「メッカ協定をイランに対抗する協定とは全く考えておらず、そうあってはならない。むしろイスラム世界のためのより広範な協定に発展することを望んでいる。イランも参加でき、他の地域諸国の参加によって協定が一層強固になることを期待している」と語った。

Russia Sanctions bill gives US President "new tool" with national security waivers, does not mean he deploys it tomorrow: Senior State Department official The legislation has raised concerns, and the Ministry of External Affairs has said that India remains firmly committed to ensuring energy security for its 1.4 billion people will continue to do so through diversified sourcing and on the basis of evolving market dynamics.
ANI | Updated: 25-09-2026 23:15 IST | Created: 25-09-2026 23:15 IST

Representative Image (Photo/Reuters) . Image Credit: ANI

SHARE

Key Takeaways
AI Summary

Analyzing article...

The Russia Sanctions Bill has given President Donald Trump another tool in his toolkit but that doesn’t necessarily mean he will deploy it, a senior US State Department official has said, noting that it provides a huge national security waiver. The legislation has raised concerns, and the Ministry of External Affairs has said that India remains firmly committed to ensuring energy security for its 1.4 billion people will continue to do so through diversified sourcing and on the basis of evolving market dynamics.
MEA also said the issue has been discussed at high levels in recent months with various US interlocutors and its potential implications for not just the bilateral relationship but also the international energy market have been very clearly articulated by the Indian side. The senior US State Department official said that while the legislation has been passed,  its practical application remains under careful evaluation.
“On the Lindsey Graham (Sanctioning Russia and Iran Act of 2026), I think what people are not understanding is Congress gave the President another tool in his toolkit. That doesn’t mean necessarily that he’s going to implement that tomorrow, but what Congress gave the President is another ability to implement sanctions where necessary. I think the idea that it’s going to happen tomorrow, I can’t tell you that. But it’s another tool in his toolbox,” the official said. Addressing questions regarding potential diplomatic friction and whether New Delhi might seek exemptions, the official emphasised that the legislation includes broad flexibility for the executive branch to navigate national security priorities.
“At the same time, they gave him a huge national security waiver, which you see in this legislation a lot. So we’ll have to wait and see in the coming days, but I think it’s, the way I would phrase it is that the President now has another tool. That does not necessarily mean he deploys it. And he has a broad national security waiver, and so we’ll see what that looks like in the coming days,” the official added. The official said that the President’s focus is on ending the Russia-Ukraine war.
“It’s been something he campaigned on and something he’s been dedicated to from the beginning. We’re looking for our friends, especially like India, to help support that effort, but I think you’ll have to stay tuned on how the bill gets implemented. But there is a broad national security waiver, so you can imagine also the President, there’s a scenario the President uses that as well.” External Affairs Minister S Jaishankar met with US Secretary of State Marco Rubio on Wednesday on the sidelines of the 81st United Nations General Assembly High-Level Week in New York and raised India’s crucial economic and strategic concerns regarding legislation targeting buyers of Russian energy.
During the bilateral talks, Jaishankar raised concerns about the Sanctioning Russia and Iran Act (SRIA), a bill aimed at imposing steep tariffs of up to 100% on major purchasers of Russian oil and gas. Sharing an update in a post on X, Jaishankar highlighted the core issues discussed during their interaction."Good to meet @SecRubio of the US #UNHighLevelWeek," Jaishankar posted. "Reiterated India's interests and concerns with regard to SRIA. Also discussed the Gulf and Ukraine situations."
Last Friday, President Trump signed the Lindsey O. Graham Sanctioning Russia and Iran Act of 2026 into law, which empowers the executive branch to levy tariffs of up to 100 per cent on nations importing Russian oil and gas, encompassing major economies like India and China. The legislation pays tribute to the late Senator Lindsey Graham, who had initially championed a sanctions framework targeting purchasers of Russian petroleum with extreme tariff rates. (ANI)

items.title: A Lapel Pin Fuels Chinese Talk of a China-Russia-Iran Triangle
items.author: Rudy Lu
items.creator: Rudy Lu
items.summary: In China’s tightly managed political information environment, seemingly trivial interactions between senior officials can become material for close reading. Netizens and commentators scrutinize seconds-long clips — who smiles, who initiates a handshake, how firmly leaders grip hands or whether they appear unusually relaxed around one …
items.summary_source: The China-Global South Project source metadata
items.body:
In China’s tightly managed political information environment, seemingly trivial interactions between senior officials can become material for close reading. Netizens and commentators scrutinize seconds-long clips — who smiles, who initiates a handshake, how firmly leaders grip hands or whether they appear unusually relaxed around one another — for clues about relationships that official readouts rarely reveal.

A brief encounter between the foreign ministers of China, Russia and Iran at the BRICS summit has become the latest example.

Video from the sidelines of the summit in New Delhi showed Chinese Foreign Minister Wang Yi chatting and laughing with his Russian and Iranian counterparts Sergei Lavrov and Abbas Araghchi. At one point, Wang reached toward a pin on Araghchi’s jacket, prompting the Iranian foreign minister to laugh. 

Araghchi’s official Telegram channel later posted a close-up of the exchange , identifying the pin as an emblem depicting the map of Iran.

The moment quickly spread across Chinese social media, landing on the trending search list of Weibo, a Chinese social media platform often compared to X, under “Wang Yi helps the Iranian foreign minister straighten his pin” (#王毅帮伊朗外长整理胸针).

A wave of Chinese-language amplification followed.

Nationalist commentary account Rongping (戎评) described Iran as “holding the advantage” and in high spirits, with China and Russia sharing the mood. 

“Such a personal and warm interaction between the Chinese and Iranian foreign ministers sends a strong signal to the outside world: China-Iran relations have long gone beyond a simple exchange of interests, and the two sides share a high degree of familiarity and trust,” it wrote.

Another online commentary said the seemingly insignificant gesture reflected a shift in the international balance of power that would make the White House “deeply uncomfortable.”

“U.S. pressure is pushing the three sides closer together,” it said. “Washington can continue to pressure the three countries separately, but it will find it increasingly difficult to stop them from exchanging resources, coordinating positions and jointly seeking alternatives.”

It said Beijing could keep channels open to Gulf Arab countries, and Moscow could draw on its close strategic ties with Tehran. Working through BRICS, the three could help Iran break its diplomatic isolation and avert a complete rupture with the United Arab Emirates and other Gulf states.

Those interpretations, however, largely reflect one strand of domestic online opinion that is sympathetic to Iran and distrustful of the United States. Beijing’s official posture has been more carefully calibrated, especially ahead of Xi Jinping’s scheduled Sept. 24 meeting with Trump in Washington.

Araghchi traveled to Beijing on Sep. 16 for talks with Wang Yi. The Chinese Foreign Ministry described Iran as a “comprehensive strategic partner” and said Beijing was prepared to help safeguard Tehran’s “legitimate rights and interests.” 

But much of Wang’s message focused on containing the conflict. He urged Iran and the United States to exercise restraint and return to negotiations, backed dialogue between Tehran and Gulf Arab governments, called for the reopening of the Strait of Hormuz and warned against the fighting spreading toward Yemen and the Red Sea.

China’s balancing role was also evident when Saudi Arabia asked Beijing to press Iran to rein in the Houthis, Reuters reported, citing three Iranian sources . China then privately urged Tehran to use its influence over the Yemeni group, whose advances threatened Saudi oil exports and shipping through the Red Sea — a vital route for Chinese trade.

PARIS, Sept 25 : Crypto exchange Bitget has stopped allowing customer withdrawals following the theft of crypto worth approximately $351.6 million in a hack, it said, adding all user funds were safe.
Bitget had noticed "unauthorised transfers" from some of its wallets on Thursday and it "temporarily suspended" customer withdrawals, Gracy Chen, CEO of the Seychelles-based company, said in a statement posted on X.
Chen said that all user funds were safe and that the loss was covered by Bitget's own funds.
"Withdrawals remain temporarily suspended as a security precaution, not because of any shortfall in funds," Chen told Reuters in an emailed statement on Friday.

Crypto exchanges have for years been subject to hacks and thefts. Last year, crypto exchange Bybit had $1.5 billion stolen in a hack, which the FBI attributed to North Korean hackers. 
North Korea routinely denies involvement in cyber hacking or crypto heists. 
Authorities have said criminals can quickly move stolen cryptocurrency across borders, without using the mainstream financial system.

items.title: India-US trade deal 90% complete, to unleash another level of ties: US State Dept official
items.summary: The India-US trade deal is “90 per cent completed,” with just final details left to be worked out, a senior US State Department official told ANI.
items.body:
India-US trade deal 90% complete, to unleash another level of ties: US State Dept official The India-US trade deal is “90 per cent completed,” with just final details left to be worked out, a senior US State Department official told ANI.
ANI | Updated: 25-09-2026 23:06 IST | Created: 25-09-2026 23:06 IST

Representative Image (Photo/Reuters). Image Credit: ANI

SHARE

Key Takeaways
AI Summary

Analyzing article...

The India-US trade deal is “90 per cent completed,” with just final details left to be worked out, a senior US State Department official told ANI. The State Department official termed the trade deal the “most sticking point” and which can potentially “unleash another level” of India-US relations.
The official said, “I would say stay tuned, which we keep saying, but we are very close. It’s like a 90-per cent-plus there and just those final things being worked out, so I hope you’re going to see something very soon on that.  And that’s really going to just unleash another level of US-India relations, something that hasn’t really – we haven’t been able to get there in decades when it comes to trade. This has always been the most sticking point in the relationship.  So I think we’re very close and it’s going to be very, very exciting when we get there.” Meanwhile, Commerce and Industry Minister Piyush Goyal on Thursday said India and the US have “done and dusted” the trade pact and will execute it once Washington gives India the right competitive advantage over its rivals in the American market.
India and the US came up with an interim framework for the trade deal in February 2026, and the negotiations are ongoing to finalise the Bilateral Trade Agreement (BTA). Speaking at the 13th Annual Forum 2026 India 3.0, the Commerce Minister said, “The nine agreements include the US, which is almost done and dusted. We have to find the right comparable competitive advantage over our competitors so that we can quickly execute the agreement.”
Earlier, US-India Business Council (USIBC) President, Ambassador (ret.) Atul Keshap said that the US and India should intensify efforts to conclude a “historic” trade agreement that lowers trade barriers and minimises tariffs, providing greater certainty to the bilateral economic and strategic partnership, according to a statement by USIBC. Calling on both governments to intensify efforts to conclude a trade agreement, Keshap said unlocking reciprocal trade would build on the record investments made in 2026 and benefit businesses in both India and the US. (ANI)

items.title: Private corporate capex estimated at Rs 3.2 lakh crore in FY27, investment momentum sustained: RBI Bulletin
items.summary: Capital expenditure by India's private corporate sector is estimated at Rs 3.2 lakh crore in 2026-27 based on the pipeline of ongoing projects, indicating continued momentum in private investment, ...
items.body:
Private corporate capex estimated at Rs 3.2 lakh crore in FY27, investment momentum sustained: RBI Bulletin Capital expenditure by India's private corporate sector is estimated at Rs 3.2 lakh crore in 2026-27 based on the pipeline of ongoing projects, indicating continued momentum in private investment, according to an article in the Reserve Bank of India's September Bulletin.
ANI | Updated: 25-09-2026 22:51 IST | Created: 25-09-2026 22:51 IST

Representative Image (Photo/Reuters). Image Credit: ANI

SHARE

Key Takeaways
AI Summary

Analyzing article...

Capital expenditure by India's private corporate sector is estimated at Rs 3.2 lakh crore in 2026-27 based on the pipeline of ongoing projects, indicating continued momentum in private investment, according to an article in the Reserve Bank of India's September Bulletin. “The phasing profile of the pipeline projects based on all channels of financing taken together, suggests that the envisaged capex is estimated at Rs 3.2 lakh crore in 2026-27, indicating sustained momentum in private investment,” the RBI said in its press release in the Bulletin.
The estimate is based on projects financed through banks and financial institutions, external commercial borrowings (ECBs), and initial public offerings (IPOs). The Bulletin article said comparable capex from these funding channels stood at Rs 2.6 lakh crore in 2025-26. It added that complete information on projects that will be sanctioned during FY27 is not yet available, and therefore the outlook is based on the pipeline of projects sanctioned in earlier years.
Private investment activity had strengthened in the previous financial year as well. The total cost of projects sanctioned by banks and financial institutions increased to a record Rs 4.4 lakh crore in 2025-26 from Rs 3.7 lakh crore in the previous year. “Private corporate investment intentions remained resilient during 2025-26 despite a challenging global environment marked by heightened geopolitical tensions, trade policy uncertainty, and volatile financial markets,” the Bulletin article said.
Infrastructure remained the biggest destination for investment, accounting for 54.2 per cent of the total cost of projects sanctioned by banks and financial institutions in 2025-26. The power sector was the major contributor, followed by roads and bridges. The bulletin said, “Infrastructure continued to dominate the investment landscape, led by the power sector.”
It also noted that greenfield projects accounted for 89.2 per cent of the total cost of projects reported by banks and financial institutions during FY26, pointing to capacity expansion by private companies. “Looking ahead, the investment outlook is expected to remain healthy, although heightened global uncertainties are likely to temper the investment sentiment,” the Bulletin article said.
The RBI clarified that views expressed in Bulletin articles are those of the authors and do not represent the views of the Reserve Bank of India. (ANI)

items.body:
Bruce Campbell, President & Portfolio Manager, StoneCastle Investment Management
Focus: Canadian Stocks

Top Picks: Altius Minerals , TMX Group , Celestica
MARKET OUTLOOK:
Inflation and interest rates are back at the centre of the market conversation. Higher oil prices have renewed inflation concerns, while U.S. bond yields have moved sharply higher and investors are pricing in further rate hikes. That backdrop can make it harder for gold to outperform, although geopolitical demand could still support it.
Our view is that rates may be approaching a peak if growth and inflation cool into 2027. The risk for investors is what slowing growth could mean for earnings. Recently, market leadership has appeared to narrow toward large caps and the Mag Seven, which we are watching closely. We remain optimistic about opportunities in equities, but increasingly selective as we look ahead.

Sign up for the Market Call Top Picks newsletter at  bnnbloomberg.ca/newsletters
TOP PICKS:
Bruce Campbell's Top Picks: Altius Minerals, TMX Group & Celestica Bruce Campbell, president & portfolio manager at StoneCastle Investment Management, shares his top stock picks to watch in the market.

Altius Minerals (ALS TSX)
A diversified portfolio of royalty assets. The company has built a portfolio of 13 mining royalty streams and 15 renewable energy royalty streams. It continues to expand and diversify its royalty base across several commodities and renewable power assets.
These long-life assets offer growth potential as mining operations expand. Altius can benefit from higher commodity prices and mine expansion without bearing the associated operating costs. The company also has a strong track record of dividend growth and an active share buyback program.
TMX Group (X TSX)
Operates Canada’s leading capital markets exchanges and is increasingly becoming a diversified global financial infrastructure and data company. Through acquisitions and organic growth, TMX has expanded internationally and increased its recurring revenue, making it less dependent on Canadian trading and financing activity. The company generates strong cash flow, supporting continued investment and dividend growth. Earlier concerns that artificial intelligence, blockchain, and decentralized finance could disrupt traditional exchanges have moderated, allowing investors to refocus on TMX’s expanding global footprint and consistent growth.
Celestica (CLS TSX)
An electronics engineering, design, and manufacturing company at the centre of the AI networking buildout. It has evolved from a traditional contract manufacturer into a key provider of data centre infrastructure.
Demand for AI computing has driven strong double-digit revenue and earnings growth, making Celestica one of Canada’s top-performing stocks. A key question for investors is whether the current buildout is a one-time event. We believe ongoing technology upgrades and growing computing needs could support demand well beyond the initial investment cycle.
The stock is not cheap on a traditional price-to-earnings basis, but its valuation appears more reasonable when measured against its expected growth.

• このデータベースへのアクセスは、最大１２社の英国企業に提供される。各社は自社の取り組みがウクライナおよび英国の防衛要件の両方に適用可能であることを示す提案書を提出しなければならない。

items.body:
Nupur Anand　Pete Schroeder　Saeed Azhar

[ニューヨーク／ワシントン ２５日 ロイター] - 米連邦準備理事会（ＦＲＢ）が、大手銀行に対する厳格な監督を発動する資産規模の基準を引き上げる計画を進めていることが、関係者４人の話で明らかになった。実現すれば、一部の銀行はコストのかかる追加規制を回避できるようになり、業界再編を促す可能性がある。

関係者によると、ＦＲＢは近く、健全性審査（ストレステスト）や流動性、資本などに関するより厳格なルールが適用される資産規模の基準について、インフレと経済成長を反映するよう見直しを提案する見通し。関係者のうち３人は、ＦＲＢが年内にも変更案を提示するとみている。

現行の規則では、銀行の資産規模が１０００億ドルに達すると規制が厳しくなり、２５００億ドル、さらに７０００億ドルで段階的に強化される。銀行側は、２０１９年に設定されたこうした基準が経済実態に即しておらず、実際のリスクに見合わない厳しい監督を強いられていると主張している。

関係者によると、ＦＲＢは最上位の基準を１兆ドル近くに引き上げるほか、より低い基準で適用される規制の一部について、適用基準を１５００億ドル近くに引き上げる計画だ。

ＦＲＢ報道官はコメントを控えた。

items.title: Trump continues voter data push despite repeated setbacks
items.author: Luc Cohen
items.creator: Luc Cohen
items.summary: President Donald Trump is pressing forward with his administration's pursuit of sensitive voter data despite repeated losses in court, seeking to identify noncitizens illegally registered to vote even though there is no evidence of widespread voter fraud.
items.body:
President Donald Trump is pressing forward with his administration's pursuit of sensitive voter data despite repeated losses in court, seeking to identify noncitizens illegally registered to vote even though there is no evidence of widespread voter fraud.
Justice Department lawyers, responding to a legal challenge to a key element of Trump's plans, urged a federal judge in Maryland on Friday not to block the Department of Homeland Security from creating lists of US citizens who are eligible to vote. Trump's fellow Republicans are fighting to keep control of Congress in the November 3 midterms .
US District Judge Paula Xinis did not immediately rule on a request by privacy advocates, who asked that she block implementation of an [USN:S0N3ZK0A9 TEXT:"executive order"] Trump signed in March, but she instructed the Justice Department to give her at least 30 days' notice before distributing the lists.
Trump's order directed DHS to create the citizen lists using data housed throughout the federal government and share them with state election officials. Under the order, state officials could face criminal prosecution if ineligible people are found to have voted in their states.
The federal government has never previously compiled any such lists. The US Constitution assigns the administration of federal elections to individual states.
The plaintiffs argue that the DHS plan to create the lists would collect information on American citizens from other federal government entities including the Social Security Administration in ways that violate privacy laws.
Trump for years has made false claims about widespread voting fraud in the US including in his loss to Democrat Joe Biden in the 2020 presidential election. Trump, who has said he is acting to protect the integrity of US elections, also has asserted that states are not doing enough to remove noncitizens and dead people from their voter rolls.
Critics have said that Trump's current drive is aimed at disenfranchising eligible Democratic-leaning voters.
They note that a federal immigration database known as SAVE, which is one of the sources that Trump's executive order directs DHS to consult in building its lists of eligible voters, has mistakenly flagged as noncitizens some Americans who are naturalized US citizens and properly registered to vote. Several Republican-led states already have checked their voter rolls against SAVE.
25 LOSSES IN COURT Most of the Trump administration's efforts to collect voter data have not succeeded.
Trump's proposed SAVE America Act, legislation that would require states to check their voter lists against the SAVE database, failed in the Republican-controlled Senate.
The Justice Department has [USN:L6N44118V TEXT:"lost 25 lawsuits"] seeking to compel states to hand over their complete voter rolls, including sensitive information such as partial Social Security numbers used to identify people. And the US Supreme Court this month [USN:S0N431004 TEXT:"declined to allow"] his push to tighten mail-in voting, which would have required states to submit lists of eligible voters to the US Postal Service.
In a [USN:L1N45H0IZ TEXT:"victory for Trump"], however, the Supreme Court on Friday allowed the administration to use a revamped version of SAVE to check voter eligibility, after a lower court blocked it in a separate case. The justices acknowledged, however, that it may be too close to the election for officials to conduct large-scale reviews of their voter rolls to remove ineligible voters.
In a July speech, Trump said without providing evidence that hundreds of thousands of noncitizens and dead people were listed as active on voter rolls, and that he directed DHS to tell states to remove them.
"We have very important elections coming up. We want those elections to be honest," Trump said.
White House spokeswoman Lauren Bis said in a statement: "Despite extreme Democrats and the media claiming it never happens, the evidence of noncitizens registering and voting in our elections continues to pile up."
'MASS DISENFRANCHISEMENT' Democrats and voting rights advocates say the administration's focus on obtaining voter data and checking for noncitizens is driven by a desire to impose obstacles on Democratic-leaning voters, rather than a genuine concern about election security.
"You can't do mass disenfranchisement without a voter file," said voting rights lawyer Marc Elias, whose firm frequently represents the Democratic Party in court.
John Hill, a lawyer at Citizens for Responsibility and Ethics in Washington, which is representing the plaintiffs challenging the DHS plans on Friday, said Trump's threat of prosecution of state officials implied that his administration would try to coerce states to use DHS's citizenship lists to purge voters.
At Friday's hearing, Justice Department lawyer Joshua Schopf told the judge that the lawsuit is premature because DHS has not yet activated the online portal through which it intends to share voter data with the states. Schopf did not say when the portal would go live or rule out activating it before the election.
GLITCHES AND CLERICAL ERRORS A Reuters review published on Wednesday found that software glitches and [USN:L1N45F0H5 TEXT:"clerical errors"] in a dozen US states run by both Democrats and Republicans may have added more than 30,000 self-declared noncitizens to the nation's voter rolls since 2000. Reuters was not able to determine how many of the noncitizens voted. Experts said the number was too small to affect elections.
In an example that Trump's White House has cited to argue that Democrats are wrong to suggest noncitizen voting is not a concern, New Jersey said in July that a technology glitch added 6,600 noncitizens to voter rolls in 2023 and 2024. The state said fewer than 400 of them actually voted, and that there was no evidence that the results of any elections were swayed.
State audits and independent studies have found voter fraud is very rare. A Reuters investigation published in July found that just 129 people had been prosecuted for noncitizen voting since a law criminalizing it was passed in 1996. The Justice Department [USN:L6N45F10R TEXT:"charged"] an additional 20 people this month.
The Department of Homeland Security has obtained voter rolls from at least 47 of the 50 US states and is reviewing them to identify noncitizens who are registered, [USN:L6N45D0T4 TEXT:"Reuters reported"] on Thursday, citing an internal email.
It remains unclear how many of those were redacted, public versions as opposed to a full accounting. The public versions often lack key personal identifying information such as partial Social Security numbers, dates of birth and driver's license numbers. DHS is using information from a commercial data broker to supplement the records, though it is not clear how much personally identifying information the department now possesses.
Even if the Trump administration prevails in court in the case heard on Friday, it is not clear whether the DHS effort to create citizenship lists would have any impact on who is eligible to vote in November. Trump's executive order directed DHS to share the lists with state election officials at least 60 days before each federal election. That would have been September 4.
items.raw_description: President Donald Trump is pressing forward with his administration's pursuit of sensitive voter data despite repeated losses in court, seeking to identify noncitizens illegally registered to vote even though there is no evidence of widespread voter fraud.

items.title: Pact with Saudi and Pakistan could expand to Muslim world, including Iran, says Turkish speaker
items.author: CNA
items.summary: Similar to NATO's Article 5, the "Mecca Joint Defence Agreement" stipulates that an attack on one ally constitutes an attack on all.
items.body:
Advertisement

World

Pact with Saudi and Pakistan could expand to Muslim world, including Iran, says Turkish speaker

Similar to NATO's Article 5, the "Mecca Joint Defence Agreement" stipulates that an attack on one ally constitutes an attack on all. 

Turkey's Foreign Minister Hakan Fidan meets with Pakistan's Deputy Prime Minister and Foreign Minister Mohammad Ishaq Dar and Saudi Arabia's Foreign Minister Prince Faisal bin Farhan Al Saud on the sidelines of the 81st United Nations General Assembly in New York City, US, on Sep 24, 2026. ANKARA: A defence pact between Türkiye, Saudi Arabia, and Pakistan could turn into a broader pact "for the Muslim world" that includes Iran, Türkiye's parliament speaker said on Friday (Sep 25), adding that it is expected to be submitted for ratification from next month.
The regional powers signed the " Mecca Joint Defence Agreement " in August, weeks before Yemen's Iran-backed Houthis launched attacks against Saudi Arabia, in reaction to the wider Iran war. Similar to NATO's Article 5, the pact stipulates that an attack on one ally constitutes an attack on all. The signatories have met to lay out the accord's parameters and assess Riyadh's needs.
"For international agreements to come into effect, parliamentary approval is needed. The meetings held as part of the agreement at the moment are preparatory meetings," Parliament Speaker Numan Kurtulmus told reporters in Ankara. "I expect this issue to come on the parliament's agenda in the coming period," he added, referring to parliament's return from recess in October.
Asked whether the pact was against Iran, Kurtulmus repeated Türkiye's position that the agreement did not target any specific country but was primarily aimed at ensuring the security of states in the region amid conflicts and Israel's "hostile policies", adding that Tehran could potentially join the pact too.
"We never see the Mecca Agreement as a pact against Iran, it must not be that way. In fact, we hope the Mecca Agreement can turn into a broader agreement for the Muslim world. Iran can join this agreement too, we hope it will become much stronger with the participation of other regional countries," he said.
Ankara has previously said it could help meet Riyadh's military needs, especially on technical issues, but officials have said any support at this stage would be largely bilateral and in the spirit of their alliance, since the joint agreement has yet to be ratified.
The military chiefs of Saudi Arabia, Türkiye and Pakistan are set to meet to discuss ways of supporting Riyadh.

items.author: ロイター
items.creator: ロイター
items.summary: ［キーウ／モスクワ　２５日　ロイター］ -
items.body:
［キーウ／モスクワ　２５日　ロイター］ - 米国は、ロシアによるウクライナ侵攻終結に向けた取り組みを協議する米国、ロシア、ウクライナ３カ国の実務者協議をアラブ首長国連邦（ＵＡＥ）で開催することを提案した。ウクライナのゼレンスキー大統領が２５日、明らかにした。

ゼレンスキー氏は対話アプリのワッツアップを通じた記者向け説明で、「米側は実務レベルでの３者形式の会合を提案した」と述べた。「日程に関する米国からの提案を待っている。米国は開催地の候補としてＵＡＥを提案した」とした。

ロシアのペスコフ大統領報道官も２５日、３カ国会合が近く開催される可能性があると述べた。ペスコフ氏は、ドミトリエフ大統領特別代表が米国を訪問しており、米交渉団と協議しているとした。関係筋によると、ドミトリエフ氏は２４日にウィトコフ、クシュナー両米代表と会談したとされる。

ゼレンスキー氏は２２日、国連総会が開かれている米ニューヨークでトランプ米大統領と会談した。会談後、エネルギー施設を対象とした停戦などについて協議したと明らかにし、ウクライナはロシアとのエネルギー停戦についていかなる形式にも応じる用意があるとしていた。

items.title: Fear of democratic socialists drives November turnout plans for some Trump voters
items.author: Julia Harte
items.creator: Julia Harte
items.summary: Seven of 18 interviewed Trump voters say left-wing gains make them more motivated to vote.
items.body:
Don Jernigan, a retiree in Virginia Beach, is disappointed by most politicians, Democrat and Republican. That includes President Donald Trump, whom he helped elect in 2024.
But Jernigan, 76, says he plans to “hold his nose” and vote for Republican candidates in November’s midterm elections. In his view, "the Democrats are now being controlled by the democratic socialists," he said, "and we’ve fought wars to keep that away from us.”
While many analysts argue that Trump's low approval ratings could dampen [USN:L1N44V0PF TEXT:"Republican turnout in November"], conversations with 18 Trump voters, including Jernigan, suggest electoral victories by progressive Democrats have energized some conservatives - even those disappointed by Trump.
Conducted with a group of Trump voters who have spoken with Reuters regularly since he returned to office , the interviews do not point to broad enthusiasm for Republican candidates themselves.
Dissatisfaction with Republican nominees for national or statewide office was rife among the group, particularly among voters in battleground states with races that could prove pivotal in deciding which party controls Congress. Chief among their concerns were the Iran war and Trump's handling of the economy.
Even so, many of those critical of the president said they would do all they can to deny Democrats control of either house of Congress.
Nearly all of the 18 voters said they were alarmed by the prospect of far-left candidates winning more seats in Congress; many expressed deep concern that progressives, if elected in meaningful numbers, would attempt to enact what they view as a socialist - or even communist - agenda in which the government tightly restricted citizens’ choices about where to spend and earn money.
Seven said that concern alone left them more motivated to vote for a conservative candidate in November.
Trump and other Republicans have falsely accused Democrats of embracing communist ideology, a charge Democrats reject as a deliberate misrepresentation of their policies.
Democratic socialists [USN:L6N43U110 TEXT:"advocate"][USN:L6N43U110 TEXT:" pursuing progressive policies"], such as government-run universal health insurance or wealth taxes, through democratic processes. In contrast, communism seeks to abolish private ownership of property and create a classless society - ideas that the democratic socialists seeking election reject.
FEARS OF SOCIALISM AND SHARIA In Georgia, where voters will elect a governor and US senator in November, David Ferguson said he hasn’t found any candidates in either party whom he can “strongly get behind” in the general election.
Yet Ferguson, 54, a mechanical engineer and account manager for an industrial supply company, said he fears that if progressive and socialist candidates got more power in Congress, they would try to exert “way too much control over markets and things that the government does not need to be involved in.”
On the other side of the state, near Savannah, insurance firm employee Amanda Taylor was so disappointed by this year’s candidates that she didn’t vote in Georgia’s primary election. But she said the rise of democratic socialists nationwide would “absolutely” help push her to the polls in November, even though she wasn't aware of any such candidates on her ballot.
Like Ferguson, Taylor, 53, worried such movements would pull the US “towards communism, where your government is dictating the groceries that you can get and you're waiting in lines for bread” and that they would require schools, bathrooms and sports teams to recognize the gender identity of transgender individuals.
Trump and other Republican leaders have pumped up their [USN:L1N4421OX TEXT:"attacks on socialism and communism"] this campaign season after a series of left-wing Democratic primary victories, including a win by Michigan US Senate nominee Abdul El-Sayed, whom the president called a "Communist loser."
El-Sayed, who faces former US Representative Mike Rogers in November, describes himself as a progressive candidate and not a socialist.
But Trump's messaging appears to be sticking - even with Republicans unhappy with the party's leadership.
In Grand Rapids, Michigan, Terry Alberta said he expects to split his ballot between Democratic and Republican candidates in November, because he leans Republican but mistrusts any candidate with an endorsement from Trump, whom he sees as increasingly volatile and prone to “silly games” with other countries.
“I don't like the radicalism on either side,” said Alberta, 65, a pilot. He said his vote will also be motivated by concern that El-Sayed secretly supports policies he has publicly disavowed, such as imposing Islamic sharia law on the US.
STRATEGIC VOTING Some voters in the group saw opportunity in the rising popularity of progressive candidates on the left. In Wisconsin’s August primary election, recent college graduate William Brown, 21, cast a "strategic" vote for Francesca Hong, a democratic socialist candidate, who narrowly lost her bid to become the state’s Democratic nominee for governor.
Had Hong won, Brown thought the Republican nominee could have defeated her more easily than a moderate Democrat - and her agenda seemed so radical that “not only would she not have been able to pass a lot of it through the legislature, but a lot of it would have been court challenged,” Brown said.
Others viewed the recent success of left-wing candidates as a warning sign about the increasingly extreme nature of US politics.
“My biggest fear is that it will be a constant impeachment of Donald Trump," said Lesa Sandberg of St. George, Utah, who runs an accounting business, rents properties and works for a Republican political action committee.
Sandberg, 58, expects the Senate to remain under Republican control, preventing new progressive US representatives from actually pushing through a socialist agenda. But for the sake of national unity, she said, she hopes Democrats “won't elect their extreme left, just like I hope we don't elect our extreme right.”
